structure: Part 8 mined all 10 traces its partition names, in full, and read both spec files (transport-and-arrival.fit.spec.js and the arrival details and transit countries blocks of snagging.fit.spec.js). Traces: transport-and-arrival.fit.spec.js has 'means of transport is the one required answer' (core and validation: renders /arrival-details, submits empty to the error state, searches Dover in the port box, picks Rail and lands on /transit-countries), 'air and sea skip transit countries' (variant: Air goes to /transporter, and a direct GET of /transit-countries 302s to /notification-hub; only Air was driven, Sea never), and 'add and remove the countries the consignment travels through' (core: Road to /transit-countries, add Belgium and Germany, remove Belgium, continue to /transporter). snagging.fit.spec.js has S19 (date hint, MOJ date picker opened, then a no-JavaScript render), S20 (port hint, default only), S21 (port search 'Heath', London Heathrow chosen, then no-JavaScript render), S22 (means of transport select options listed in place), S23 (transport identification hint, default only), S24 (transit search 'Bel', suggestions open, no-JavaScript render) and S25 (search and add Belgium then Germany, no-JavaScript render). Pages, in journey order: (1) /arrival-details 'Arrival details', caption 'Transport and arrival', always shown after the consignment details in section 3 of the task list; pointer trace means-of-transport action 53 (default) and 67 (error); (2) /transit-countries 'Which countries will the consignment travel through?', caption 'Movement', shown only when the means of transport is Rail or Road; pointer trace add-and-remove action 58 (default) and 83 (two countries). The next page, /transporter, belongs to part 9 and is only named here as a destination. Each page was read from its snapshot DOM (main innerText, outerHTML, controls, embedded JSON data) and the network log; no page was reached by a wrong pointer. Neither page made a data call: the port list and the transit country list are embedded in each page as JSON, and the only requests are the page GETs and form POSTs. No germinal-products variant of either page was walked.

Draft

claims.quote: The expected date of arrival at the port of entry. For example, 27/3/2026

claims.statement: The arrival date is entered as day/month/year with slashes in one text box: the test typed '11/12/2026' and the form posted arrivalDateAtPort=11/12/2026.
claims.quote: arrivalDateAtPort=11%2F12%2F2026

claims.statement: The arrival date uses the Ministry of Justice date picker: a 'Choose date' button beside the text box opens a calendar dialog with previous and next year and month buttons, a month-year title, and 'Select' and 'Close' buttons.
claims.quote: <div class="moj-datepicker" data-module="moj-date-picker" ... Choose date ... Previous year ... Previous month ... Next month ... Next year ... Select ... Close
claims.note: A tested government library (MOJ Frontend), not GOV.UK Frontend; the field is not the GOV.UK Date input component.

claims.statement: When opened, the date picker shows the current month and marks today: on 27 November 2026 it opened on 'November 2026' with Friday 27 November 2026 as today and the focused day.
claims.quote: title=November 2026 | today=Friday 27 November 2026

claims.statement: The date picker only allows dates from 7 days before today to 6 months after today: recorded on 27 November 2026 it set a minimum of 20/11/2026 and a maximum of 27/5/2027, and announced earlier days as excluded.
claims.ref: trace transport-and-arrival--arrival-details-means-of-transport-is-the-one-required-answer.zip action 53, div.moj-datepicker data-min-date and data-max-date
claims.quote: data-min-date="20/11/2026" data-max-date="27/5/2027" ... Excluded date, Thursday 19 November 2026
claims.note: The offsets (minus 7 days, plus 6 months) are read from the two dates against the recording date; the trace shows the dates, not the rule that made them.

The arrival details page is reached directly by URL in every trace, after the consignment details; the tests describe it as section 3 of the task list (transport and arrival), but no trace shows the task list link that leads to it.

claims.note: The spec comment says transit countries is for rail and road only, which matches what the traces show for Rail, Road and Air.
